text: During recent public health crises, many people rejected expert advice in favour of claims they had read online or heard from friends. In my view, declining trust in science has causes both in the way information spreads and in the way scientists communicate, and restoring it requires changes from researchers, technology companies and schools alike.

One major cause is the flood of misleading information on social media. False claims are usually simpler and more emotional than scientific explanations, so they spread faster and reach more people. At the same time, scientists have sometimes contributed to the problem. Research findings are often presented in language that ordinary people cannot follow, and when early advice changes as new evidence emerges, the public may see this as a sign of incompetence rather than as the normal process of science. Occasional scandals involving falsified data or undeclared conflicts of interest further damage confidence.

Several steps could help to rebuild trust. First, scientists should explain their work in plain language and be open about uncertainty, making it clear that changing conclusions reflect progress, not error. Second, social media companies should label misleading content and promote reliable sources, particularly on health issues. Finally, schools should teach students how scientific knowledge is produced and how to judge whether a source is reliable, so that the next generation is better equipped to recognise misinformation.

In conclusion, public distrust of science stems both from the speed at which false information spreads and from weaknesses in scientific communication. Clearer explanations, responsible online platforms and better education in critical thinking can gradually restore the confidence that society needs.

strengths.en: The writer blames both social media and scientists themselves — a complete, honest answer.

note.en: Introduction: a recent example and a thesis where both suggestions in the task become two causes, with the players in the solution named at once.
note.kk: Кіріспе: жақын өткеннен мысал және тапсырмадағы екі нұсқа екі себеп ретінде берілген тезис, шешімге қатысатындар бірден аталған.

note.en: Causes: misinformation on social media and scientists’ own failings — language, changing advice, scandals.
note.kk: Себептер: әлеуметтік желідегі жалған ақпарат және ғалымдардың өз қателіктері — тілі, ұсыныстардың өзгеруі, жанжалдар.

note.en: Conclusion: causes and solutions in brief, with no new ideas.
